models_evaluated: Tufts-PACE CPM Registry cardiovascular prognostic models

links.outcome: Between-study variation in AUC across external validations of the same model
links.effect: Mean tau of 0.055 (SD 0.015); with tau=0.05 the 95% prediction interval for AUC in a new setting is at least +/-0.1 regardless of validation count.
links.quote: If τ$$ \tau $$ = 0.05, then the 95% prediction interval for the AUC in a new setting has a width of at least +/-$$ +/- $$ 0.1, no matter how many validations have been done.

links.outcome: Heterogeneity of AUC across settings due to population, standard of care, and predictor definitions
links.effect: Large heterogeneity among validated AUCs gives great irreducible uncertainty in predicting AUC in a new setting; frequentist methods underestimate this uncertainty with fewer than 5 validations.
links.quote: Due to large heterogeneity among the validated AUC values of a CPM, there is great irreducible uncertainty in predicting the AUC in a new setting.

unlisted_practices: Using an empirical Bayes prior on between-study heterogeneity to form prediction intervals for AUC in a new setting

screen.reason: Analyzes heterogeneity across 1603 external validations of 469 clinical prediction models to evaluate an empirical Bayes method for anticipating AUROC uncertainty prior to new setting deployment.

primary.practice: empirical Bayes adjustment for model transportability and external validation uncertainty
